::: {#thm-r-squared-slr}
#### $R^2$ of a simple linear regression

For the OLS fit of a simple linear regression,
with $S_{xx} > 0$ and $S_{yy} > 0$ (@def-centered-sums),
$R^2$ is the square of the
[Pearson correlation coefficient](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-pearson-r) $r$
of the $x_i$ and $y_i$,
and so lies between 0 and 1:

$$
\begin{aligned}
R^2 &= r^2, &
0 \le R^2 &\le 1.
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

::: proof

This is the solution to @exr-r-squared-slr,
which uses the residual sum of squares from @exr-rss-ols-fit.

:::
